title: Channel cohorting and upgrade safety matrix for runtime + surfaces
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a pragmatic, testable channel cohorting strategy and an explicit upgrade safety matrix that covers the runtime, REST API, official SDKs, and Console surface. The outcome should be an operational spec + automation checklist that the SRE and Release teams can run before any channel promotion (edge->stable->lts), and a machine-readable matrix used by CI to gate cross-surface compatibility tests.

Why: We currently have ad-hoc checks for upgrades which cause customer-visible regressions during cross-surface rollouts (e.g., runtime change + SDK surface mismatch). This ticket centralizes the compatibility rules and maps them to concrete rollout gates and automated preflight checks.

Scope:
- Define cohorting buckets and routing semantics for customers during promotions (canary / cohort % / shadowing).
- Produce compatibility statements for: runtime binary/API semantic contract, REST API minor/patch compatibility, JS/Python/Go SDK major/minor policies, Console feature toggles and dashboard schema compatibility.
- Design a YAML (single-level key-value) upgrade safety matrix that CI can ingest to run targeted integration suites.
- Specify rollout gates (observability thresholds, error budget burn, acceptance on customer canaries) and rollback triggers.
- Implementation plan for an automated preflight runbook and a follow-up CLI to mark channel promotions.

Non-goals: Full integration automation for Dedicated/private upgrades (will scope in follow-up ticket), changing semantic versioning itself (we assume existing semver policy).
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable spec describing cohort buckets and routing rules is in the release repo.
A CI-consumable YAML safety matrix exists and maps runtime -> API -> SDK -> Console compatibility assertions.
Automated preflight pipeline that runs smoke+integration tests against a staged cohort is defined and documented.
Rollout gate checklist with quantifiable thresholds is published and integrated with alerting dashboards.
Security review notes captured and any required mitigations recorded before promotion to LTS channel.
decisions: Adopt three cohort buckets: canary (0.1-1%), cohort-A (5-10%), cohort-B (25%), then global rollout.
Compatibility matrix will express compatibility as one of: compatible, compatible-with-deprecation, incompatible. CI will fail for 'incompatible' entries.
Minor runtime releases may be promoted to stable when API contract tests pass and SDK smoke runs succeed; LTS promotion requires additional canary duration + manual signoff.
SDKs will follow a strict minor/backcompat policy: minor runtime changes that alter client-visible tokenization or response envelopes require SDK minor bumps and consumer-facing changelog entries.
open_risks: Edge cases where Console relies on undocumented API fields could break without detection; requires schema contracts for dashboard payloads.
Customer-specific Dedicated deployments may not be included in cohorting; we need a separate enrollment flow to avoid surprises.
Runtime ABI shims for quantized kernels may hide behavioral differences that unit tests won't catch.
implementation_steps: Draft cohorting semantics doc and routing header format (X-Redwood-Channel / X-Redwood-Cohort).
Design YAML schema for the safety matrix and implement a parser in release-ci that produces test jobs.
Extend integration test suite to run per-matrix entry (runtime+api+sdk+console permutations) and report pass/fail with trace ids.
Add rollout gate monitors: per-route token error rate, 99th latency change, cost per token delta, and qualitative eval regressions for a small prompt corpus.
Build a release CLI: `rwd release promote --channel lts --matrix path/to/matrix.yaml` that triggers preflight and records artifacts.
